title: driver/plan.json (the engine's answer to "plan this session")
description: The work plan a driven session runs, under .dabbler/runs/s<N>/driver/plan.json: what the session will do and the ordered steps -- each with an id, the files it expects to touch, and at least one check that proves it. The driver declares the session from `task`, then issues the steps one at a time and measures each report against its step. A check is argv, never a shell string, and the driver runs it rather than reading it: code and tests are compiled and run, never interpreted. Validated before it is written; a file that fails validation on read is refused.

schema_version.description: Frozen at v1. A reader that finds any other value refuses the file rather than interpreting it.

task.description: What this session will do -- the text the declaration records.

releasable.description: An older plan's member, read as it was recorded and ignored: an ordinary session never publishes, and a release is a session of its own, headed `(release: <version>)` in the session plan.

release.description: An older plan's member, read as it was recorded and ignored. A plan answered now that names it is refused at acceptance: an ordinary session never publishes, and a release is a session of its own, headed `(release: <version>)` in the session plan.

hold_release.description: An older plan's member, read as it was recorded and ignored. A plan answered now that names it is refused at acceptance: an ordinary session never publishes, so there is nothing to hold; a person stops a release session's publish with `dabbler session hold-release`.

non_goals.description: What this session will NOT do: the exclusions its section of the session plan states, or the nearest concrete boundary of the task where it states none. Judged at acceptance, where a plan without at least one is refused naming the member -- an engine that cannot name one has not understood the scope -- and the reviewer holds the work to the list. Optional here so that a plan recorded before the member existed is read as it was recorded: the record is never refused after the fact.

text.description: The non-goal as it was declared, word for word: the drop names a declared one or it is refused.

reason.description: Why the work falsified it, given when it was dropped.

dropped_non_goals.description: The non-goals this session declared and then dropped, each with the reason given. A non-goal is declared before the work and the work can falsify it; dropping it is a scope change recorded as one, rather than a true finding disputed away. The work is no longer held to these, and the reviewer is shown both lists -- so what it judges is the reason. Written only by `session plan amend --drop-non-goal`, which is drop-only: nothing adds a non-goal mid-session, because that would put finished, reviewed work retroactively out of scope.

repositories.description: Other repositories of this SOLUTION that the plan needs to exist. Each is placed when the plan is accepted -- created beside this one with a `solution-dependencies.json` declaring which solution it is in and its own id, and nothing else -- so that finishing this repository leaves the next one visible in the Solution Explorer instead of leaving the operator to remember it. One that already declares itself is left exactly as it is. It declares no dependency: what this repository takes is declared on the edge that takes it, and placing a repository never invents one. Optional, and absent in the ordinary single-repository session.

id.description: Its stable repository id -- the name a `producedBy` uses for it.

path.description: Where to place it, relative to this repository's root. Defaults to the first declared search path, which is where the assembly already looks.

id.description: Unique within the plan; the reader refuses a duplicate.

ask.description: What the step does, in words the driver hands back as the instruction's `ask`.

files.description: The files the step expects to create or change, repository-relative. A report for the step must list each of them.

argv.description: The program and its arguments, spawned with no shell. Exit 0 proves the step.

checks.description: What proves the step, and at least one: a step with no check is a step the driver would close on the engine's word. A step whose product is prose still has a mechanical check -- that the file exists and is not empty, that a link resolves, that a generator agrees.

modules.description: Read by nothing. A plan recorded while docs/modules.yaml was read may name the module(s) it worked in; it is accepted and the member ignored, and the plan ask no longer mentions it.

reason.description: Read by nothing. The member stays so a plan recorded while it was asked for is still read.
